method: production build; 100 sequential node-kind edits dispatched as native change events on the node-kind control; latency is input-event timestamp to the task after the frame that paints React's commit; idleFrameMs is the engine's median idle requestAnimationFrame-to-post-paint cadence.

recorded_failure.measured: p95 335 ms against a 100 ms target
recorded_failure.bottleneck: WebKit paints the canvas SVG (250 nodes / 500 edges) roughly five times slower than Chromium for the same DOM; the authoritative edit handler is ~1 ms, so the cost is engine rasterization of the edge layer, not application JavaScript.
recorded_failure.scoped_fix: Reduce the painted edge payload for admitted-size graphs on engines without efficient SVG rasterization, for example by virtualizing edges to the viewport, batching edge label rendering, or moving the edge layer to a canvas renderer. This is not yet implemented.
recorded_failure.reviewed_decision: The strict PERF-02 assertion is enforced on chromium, where the target is met with margin, and recorded on the other engines. Thresholds and corpus size are unchanged.

supplementary_measurements.scope: PERF-08 and PERF-03 recorded at the Studio head; no threshold, workload or assertion was changed and the CI PERF-01/PERF-02 results above are unchanged

PERF-08.definition: initial core route = every JavaScript file dist/index.html loads eagerly (script src and modulepreload); lazy chunks and workers are excluded from the core figure and reported separately

PERF-03.admission: not admitted: the owner per-graph ceiling is 256 nodes / 1024 edges (see corpus.owner_ceiling) and the benchmark harness caps at 512 nodes / 2048 edges, so the 1000/2000 workload cannot be produced or admitted; measured at the admitted ceiling instead
PERF-03.method: same production harness as PERF-01/02 (?benchmark=256x1024 against a vite preview of the head production build); first-useful-render is navigation start to the first painted designer graph, sampled over five cold page loads per engine (p95 = highest of five); the 100-edit workload was then run once for context
PERF-03.environment: local headless run through the orchestration browser-runtime wrapper on AMD Ryzen 5 5600X (12 threads), Linux 7.0.0, Node 24.16.0; Firefox ran with MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX=1; this is not the GitHub-hosted CI hardware that produced the PERF-01/02 rows
not_measured: webkit (not run locally; the CI WebKit job runs only the 250x500 PERF-01/02 workload)
PERF-03.note: The edit latency at 256x1024 is recorded for context only; PERF-02 is defined at 250x500 and its recorded results are unchanged.
